title: reduce streaming token latency: tighten token loop, adaptive flush cadence, backpressure + kernel/scheduling tweaks
author: Priya Desai
description: Motivation: Streaming token latency observed in several production workloads shows a long tail caused by the token emission loop cadence, aggressive flush timing, and suboptimal backpressure handling when the runtime switches scheduling modes. This PR reduces median and p95 per-token latency by combining: 1) tightening the streaming token loop (eliminate micro-sleeps and opportunistic async progress), 2) introducing an adaptive flush cadence driven by observed output rate and NVTX-friendly timers, 3) improving backpressure signals between request inflight queues and scheduler to avoid batching stalls, and 4) two small kernel selection heuristics to prefer low-latency kernels for short sequence streams. Changes are intentionally small-scoped and guarded behind a runtime feature flag (STREAM_ADAPTIVE_FLUSH). Checklist: - [x] Measure baseline across perf-canary workloads - [x] Implement token loop and flush logic - [x] Add backpressure signaling and tests - [x] Kernel selector heuristics + existing unit tests - [x] Perf regression safety (flags + rollout) This description includes: rationale, approach, micro-benchmarks, and rollout notes. See the commits for granular changes and the review comments for discussion notes.
commits: c1a4b2f: implement adaptive flush cadence and expose STREAM_ADAPTIVE_FLUSH flag
f9e8d7a: refactor streaming token loop to use non-blocking progress + remove micro-sleeps
d3b2a1c: add backpressure channel between inflight queue and scheduler; improve metrics
b4c57de: kernel selector: prefer low-latency kernels for short sequence lengths
e7f3a90: perf tests and unit tests for backpressure + flush cadence
a0f12b4: docs: changelog entry and rollout instructions
review_comments: Evan Brooks (2025-01-13): Can you include a config toggle for the adaptive timer so we can A/B in Dedicated? Priya: added STREAM_ADAPTIVE_FLUSH and documented rollout behavior.

Marisol Vega (2025-01-14): The non-blocking progress looks good, but ensure we don't spin CPU at high QPS. Suggest a backoff floor. Priya: implemented an exponential floor and smoke-tested at 100k rps.

Konstantin Petrov (2025-01-15): Kernel heuristic seems heuristic-y; how do we avoid regressions on long sequences? Priya: heuristic applies only when avg_input_length < 64 and predicted tokens per request < 128; guarded by feature flag.
Evan Brooks (2025-01-16): CI flake on perf test noise, re-ran. Priya: adjusted test harness to use deterministic seeds and NVTX markers.

Marisol Vega (2025-01-18): Approve after adding metrics for flush cadence and queue occupancy. Priya: added metrics: streaming.flush_interval_ms, streaming.backpressure_level, streaming.kvcache.hits_during_flush.
Release Manager (2025-01-20): Verified no change to public API surface and added to RC notes.
perf_summary: Benchmarks run on perf-canary V100 and A100 pools across chat and single-turn generation. Median per-token latency reduced by ~18% (A100) and ~12% (V100). P95 improved by ~24% (A100) and ~16% (V100). End-to-end tail improvements are larger for low-latency short-turn chat workloads (up to 35% p99 reduction). KV-cache hit workloads see an additional ~6% reduction because flush cadence aligns with cache warming.
safety_and_rollback: Changes are feature-flagged (STREAM_ADAPTIVE_FLUSH, STREAM_LOW_LAT_KERNELS) and default off for Dedicated/private until the RC rollout. Rollback plan: flip flags to false and redeploy; metrics instrumented to detect regression in token latency and throughput. No DB or schema changes.
compatibility_notes: Runtime flags gate behavior; no protocol or API changes. Streaming wire format unchanged. SDKs don't require updates.
release_notes: Improved streaming token emission latency by tightening the token loop, adding adaptive flush cadence, better backpressure handling, and a short-sequence low-latency kernel preference. Enabled behind STREAM_ADAPTIVE_FLUSH and STREAM_LOW_LAT_KERNELS flags. Performance: median token latency -18% (A100), p95 -24% (A100).
testing: Unit tests added for backpressure signaling and kernel selection. End-to-end perf tests added under tests/perf/streaming_latency.py. Manual canary run on perf-canary pool and staged rollout to RC cluster. CI: linux-unit, linux-integration, perf (flaky test retried once).
notes: Follow-ups: 1) evaluate dynamic kernel switching during long-running streams (ENG-4990), 2) integrate flush cadence metric into Console dashboards, 3) explore microbatching tweak to further reduce p99 for tiny tokens.
